declared.title: Adherence to Personal Resolutions Across Time, Culture, and Goal Domains
declared.foundIn: reports/choose-your-struggle/counter-evidence.md (card 15); Crossref search « Woolley Giurge Fishbach intrinsic motivation adherence personal resolutions » (preprint), then OpenAlex search of its title (2026-11-26)

population: US adults on their New Year's resolutions for a year, adults in China over a month, US adults' steps, and a US experiment over 24 h (4 studies)

findings.text: Over a year, US adults' intrinsic motivation (the pursuit felt as an end in itself) predicted adherence to their resolutions more than extrinsic motivation

support.sentence: In a year-long longitudinal study, U.S. adults set extrinsic New Year's resolutions, but intrinsic motivation predicted adherence to these goals more than extrinsic motivation (Study 1).

findings.text: The same held among adults in China over one month, and for the steps US adults copied from their phone app for the 2 weeks before the survey (cross-sectional: motivation was measured after the walking)

support.sentence: These findings emerged among adults in China (Study 2) and when measuring goal adherence objectively using the number of steps U.S. adults walked over 2 weeks (Study 3).

findings.text: Told to have fun with a health app rather than to judge its usefulness, US adults scanned more products with it over the next 24 h (d = 0.21)

support.sentence: Indeed, increasing intrinsic (vs. extrinsic) motivation increased U.S. adults' goal adherence (Study 4).

limits: one laboratory (as woolley-2016-fun and woolley-2022-discomfort); studies 1 and 2 not preregistered, studies 3 and 4 preregistered
analysed: 2,000 (study 1, 577 left after a year: 71% lost, missing data by FIML), 267 of 500 in China a month later, 439, 763
adherence self-reported (1-7) in studies 1 and 2; study 3: steps of the 14 days before the survey, copied from the app, two screenshots checking part of them
the only experiment (study 4) lasts 24 h with one health app, d = 0.21; its sample was enlarged after a smaller first effect (preregistered extension)
intrinsic motivation is the pursuit felt as enjoyable: enjoying the path, not accepting pain; extrinsic = useful, important (the value of the result)
no sample from the Middle East or North Africa; one sample from China, where the extrinsic scale is unreliable (alpha .41): a weak comparison
